prop:q-heat-equation-exists: Proposition Existence and uniqueness for the q-heat equation. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a quantum observable universe with initial data u_0 \colon \mathcal{S} \to \mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{C}}. There exists a formal solution u(t) of the q-heat equation \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u with u(0) = u_0.
prf:q-heat-equation-exists: Proof Proof of existence and uniqueness for the q-heat equation. Formal solution: u(t) = \exp(-t \Delta_q) u_0 = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{(-t \Delta_q)^n}{n!} u_0, which lives in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}) \otimes u_0 as a formal power series in t. On Peter--Weyl isotypic components \pi_j(u_0), the solution is the eigenfunction expansion u(t) = \sum_j e^{-\lambda_j(q) t} \pi_j(u_0) (the Peter--Weyl decomposition of the heat kernel, proved in the information-theory chapter), which is a finite sum on each irrep summand and therefore exists categorically without convergence hypotheses. Over \mathbb{C} the sum converges to a smooth solution; over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p the formal sum has the same categorical meaning.
prop:q-heat-equation-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of solutions of the q-heat equation. Let V be a complex vector space that is the algebraic direct sum V = \bigoplus_j V_j of finite-dimensional subspaces, and let \Delta_q \colon V \to V be a linear operator with \Delta_q(V_j) \subseteq V_j for every j. (For the function algebra of a quantum observable universe the V_j are the Peter–Weyl isotypic components and \Delta_q is the q-Laplacian of prop:q-heat-equation-exists.) Write \pi_j \colon V \to V_j for the projections. A solution of the q-heat equation \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u on [0, T) is a map u \colon [0, T) \to V such that every \pi_j u is differentiable and \tfrac{d}{dt}\, \pi_j u = -\Delta_q\, \pi_j u.

Then for every u_0 \in V there is exactly one solution with u(0) = u_0, namely

  \pi_j u(t) \;=\; \exp\!\bigl(-t\, \Delta_q|_{V_j}\bigr)\, \pi_j u_0
  \qquad \text{for all } j .
prf:q-heat-equation-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of q-heat equation solutions. Because each V_j is \Delta_q-stable, \pi_j \Delta_q = \Delta_q \pi_j, so the equation splits into one linear ODE on each finite-dimensional space V_j.

Existence. The displayed formula gives a differentiable curve in V_j with \tfrac{d}{dt}\pi_j u = -\Delta_q \pi_j u. Only the finitely many j with \pi_j u_0 \neq 0 give a nonzero component, so u(t) lies in the algebraic direct sum V.

Uniqueness. Let u be any solution with u(0) = u_0 and fix j. Put w(t) = \exp(t\,\Delta_q|_{V_j})\, \pi_j u(t). Then

  \dot w(t) \;=\; \exp(t\,\Delta_q|_{V_j})\,\bigl(\Delta_q\, \pi_j u(t) + \tfrac{d}{dt}\pi_j u(t)\bigr) \;=\; 0 ,

so w is constant, equal to w(0) = \pi_j u_0. Hence \pi_j u(t) = \exp(-t\,\Delta_q|_{V_j})\,\pi_j u_0. This holds for every j, and u(t) is determined by its projections. \square

No semisimplicity of \Delta_q is used: the matrix exponential on each V_j handles a non-diagonalisable block as well.
def:categorical-laplace:
Definition Categorical Laplace transform. The categorical Laplace transform is the monoidal functor

  \mathcal{L}\colon \bigl(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \ast_q\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \bigl(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \cdot\bigr)

defined by the Hopf pairing against the real exponential grouplike \exp_q(-s\cdot) \in G(\mathcal{H}_q):

  \mathcal{L}[f](s) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\exp_q(-s\cdot)  \cdot  f\bigr).
rem:categorical-laplace-remark: Remark The Laplace transform as a mate of the comultiplication. The categorical Laplace transform \mathcal{L} intertwines q-convolution with pointwise product; this characterises it uniquely as the mate of the comultiplication \Delta_q on \mathcal{H}_q.
rem:categorical-laplace-transform-proper: Remark Base-ring independence of the categorical Laplace transform. The transform \mathcal{L} applies over any base ring R where \mathcal{H}_q supports the grouplike. Evaluating the pairing against the archimedean realisation recovers the integral \int_0^\infty e^{-st} f(t) dt.
rem:categorical-laplace-three-contexts: Remark The categorical Laplace transform across \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p. Over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathcal{L} becomes a finite sum over the grouplike spectrum. Over \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathcal{L} is a continuous functional on locally constant functions. Over \mathbb{C}_p, \mathcal{L} extends to rigid-analytic functions on the open disc.
rem:categorical-laplace-q-heat-resolvent: Remark The categorical Laplace transform and the q-heat resolvent. The Laplace transform converts the q-heat equation into the spectral equation s \hat{u}(s) - u_0 = -\widehat{\Delta_q} \hat{u}(s). This yields the resolvent of the q-Laplacian, \hat{u}(s) = (s + \widehat{\Delta_q})^{-1} u_0.
prop:categorical-laplace-exists: Proposition Existence of the categorical Laplace transform. The categorical Laplace transform exists as a monoidal functor (\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \ast_q) \to (\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \cdot).
prf:categorical-laplace-exists: Proof Proof of existence of the categorical Laplace transform. The grouplike \exp_q(-s\cdot) \in G(\mathcal{H}_q) exists by (existence of \exp_q, proved later in this chapter). The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) \to \mathbf{1} exists by the rigid structure and Frobenius pairing. For each s, the morphism \mathcal{L}[f](s) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\exp_q(-s\cdot) \cdot f) is therefore a well-defined element of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A). Functoriality in f and monoidality (intertwining \ast_q with \cdot) follow from the coproduct axiom on \exp_q.
prop:categorical-laplace-unique: Proposition Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform. The categorical Laplace transform is uniquely characterised as the mate of the coproduct \Delta_q on \mathcal{H}_q under the Frobenius pairing.
prf:categorical-laplace-unique: Proof Proof of uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform. Two monoidal functors \mathcal{L}, \mathcal{L}' with the same intertwining property are determined by their values on the generator \exp_q(-s\cdot) (uniqueness of \exp_q, proved later in this chapter): fixing \mathcal{L}[\exp_q(-s\cdot)] pins down the functor on all of \mathcal{H}_q by monoidality. The Frobenius-pairing mate of \Delta_q is unique up to isomorphism, hence \mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{L}'.
def:categorical-fourier:
Definition Categorical Fourier transform. The categorical Fourier transform pairs against the unitary grouplike \exp_q(i\xi\cdot):

  \mathcal{F}\colon \bigl(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \ast_q\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \bigl(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), \cdot\bigr), \qquad \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\exp_q(i\xi\cdot) \cdot f\bigr),

where \xi ranges over the categorical spectrum \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A^\vee).
rem:categorical-fourier-transform-proper: Remark Realisations of the categorical Fourier transform: Peter--Weyl, Wick rotation, and base rings. When G = \mathrm{SU}_q(2), the Tannaka--Krein reconstruction identifies \mathcal{F} with the Peter--Weyl decomposition. Applying \mathcal{F} to the q-heat equation diagonalises the q-Laplacian on each Peter--Weyl summand, producing the Peter--Weyl heat kernel. The algebraic Fourier transform via Peter--Weyl projection functions identically over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, and \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}].
rem:categorical-fourier-brings-dft: Remark Abelian instance: the Bring's-surface DFT and Briggs--Klein smoothness. When G = C_5 and q = 1, the transform degenerates to the classical discrete Fourier transform on \mathbb{Z}/5. Fourier decomposition separates spectral components, rendering collision invisible and securing the smoothness of the Briggs--Klein chart on Bring's surface.
prop:categorical-fourier-exists:
Proposition Existence of the categorical Fourier transform. For the ground ring R_q = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], the Peter–Weyl decomposition of the quantum observable universe yields a categorical Fourier transform \mathcal{F}: a monoidal functor intertwining the q-convolution with the pointwise product on irreducible components,

  \mathcal{F}(f \ast_q g) = \mathcal{F}(f) \cdot \mathcal{F}(g).
prf:categorical-fourier-exists:
Proof Proof of existence of the categorical Fourier transform. The proof strategy is constructive. Form the operator \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\exp_q(i \xi \cdot) \cdot f) using the categorical trace and the quantum exponential. This construction satisfies the monoidal functor properties required for the categorical Fourier transform.

Identical to (existence of categorical Laplace transform) with the substitution s \mapsto -i\xi: the grouplike \exp_q(i\xi\cdot) exists for every categorical spectrum value \xi \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A^\vee), and pairing against the Markov trace yields a well-defined monoidal functor. Equivalently, \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) = \mathcal{L}[f](-i\xi) (Wick rotation) inherits existence from the Laplace case.
rem:categorical-fourier-exists-harmonic: Remark Projections and harmonic analysis on A. Concretely, given the family of irreducible representations (irreps), the Fourier transform provides a family of projections, each isolating the component of an endomorphism on a given irrep. This structural existence theorem underpins the harmonic analysis on the categorical Frobenius–Hopf algebra A.
prop:categorical-fourier-unique: Proposition Uniqueness of the categorical Fourier transform. The categorical Fourier transform \mathcal{F}, once it exists, is unique up to natural monoidal isomorphism: any two functors \mathcal{F} and \mathcal{F}' that intertwine the q-convolution over the algebra \mathcal{A} with the pointwise product on the spectrum of irreducible representations and preserve the Peter–Weyl projections are equivalent.
prf:categorical-fourier-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of the categorical Fourier transform. The strategy leverages the Peter-Weyl theorem. By requiring the transform to agree with the dual action \mathcal{L}[f](-i \xi) on irreducible components, the representation ring structure uniquely pins down the labels and forces the uniqueness of the monoidal functor \mathcal{F}.

Wick rotation inherits uniqueness from (uniqueness of categorical Laplace transform): \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) = \mathcal{L}[f](-i\xi) for a unique \mathcal{L} gives a unique \mathcal{F}. Independently, the Peter--Weyl decomposition is unique up to permutation of irreducibles (which is a change of labelling, not of the functor).
rem:categorical-fourier-unique-invarianc: Remark Harmonic decomposition as an intrinsic invariant. Uniqueness guarantees that the harmonic decomposition of physical states in the quantum observable universe does not depend on the choice of basis or the specific representative of the functor, but is an intrinsic topological invariant of the category.
prose:intro-q-resolvent-wick: Define the q-resolvent R_q(s) = (s + \widehat{\Delta_q})^{-1} as a categorical Laplace transform of the q-heat semigroup. The categorical Wick rotation collapses the Laplace and Fourier transforms into a single grouplike pairing against \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q) evaluated at s or i\xi.
def:q-resolvent:
Definition q-Resolvent (categorical). Let \widehat{\Delta_q} be the q-Laplacian acting on \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), and let s \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A) be a categorical spectral parameter. The q-resolvent is the morphism

  R_q(s) \;=\; \bigl(s + \widehat{\Delta_q}\bigr)^{-1} \;\in\; \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A),

defined wherever s + \widehat{\Delta_q} is invertible in the convolution algebra \mathcal{H}_q.
rem:q-resolvent-properties:
Remark Realisations of R_q(s): Laplace characterisation, resolvent identity, Peter--Weyl poles, and base rings. R_q(s) is the categorical Laplace transform, in the time variable t, of the q-heat semigroup \exp(-t \widehat{\Delta_q}):

  R_q(s) \;=\; \mathcal{L}\bigl[\exp(-t \widehat{\Delta_q})\bigr](s).

The first resolvent identity R_q(s_1) - R_q(s_2) = (s_2 - s_1) R_q(s_1) R_q(s_2) is the Hopf-algebraic mate of the comultiplication axiom on \mathcal{H}_q. Under the categorical Fourier transform with G = \mathrm{SU}_q(2), the resolvent diagonalises over irreducibles:

  R_q(s) \;=\; \bigoplus_{j \in \widehat{G}} \frac{\pi_j}{s + \lambda_j(q)},

where \lambda_j(q) = [j]_q[j+1]_q (1 - q^{-1})^2.

The resolvent acts as the s-domain Green's function of the q-heat flow. Contour integration around a pole at -\lambda_j(q) extracts the projector \pi_j onto the j-isotypic subspace.
prop:q-resolvent-exists: Proposition Existence of the q-resolvent. For s \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A) outside the categorical spectrum of \widehat{\Delta_q}, the q-resolvent R_q(s) = (s + \widehat{\Delta_q})^{-1} exists as an endomorphism of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A).
prf:q-resolvent-exists:
Proof Proof of existence of the q-resolvent. Two constructions:

  1. Laplace transform. By (existence of categorical Laplace transform), \mathcal{L}[\exp(-t \widehat{\Delta_q})](s) is well-defined for every s in the domain of the Laplace pairing. The resulting morphism equals R_q(s) by the spectral identity \int_0^\infty e^{-(s + \lambda)t} dt = (s + \lambda)^{-1}.

  2. Peter--Weyl diagonal. Under the Fourier decomposition of \widehat{\Delta_q} with eigenvalues \lambda_j(q), define R_q(s) = \bigoplus_j \pi_j / (s + \lambda_j(q)) on each isotypic summand. This is well-defined whenever s + \lambda_j(q) \ne 0 for every j — i.e. outside the categorical spectrum. The direct sum converges formally in \mathrm{End}(\bigoplus_j V_j \otimes V_j^\vee).

Both constructions yield the same morphism.
prop:q-resolvent-unique: Proposition Uniqueness of the q-resolvent. The q-resolvent R_q(s) is the unique morphism satisfying (s + \widehat{\Delta_q}) \circ R_q(s) = \mathrm{id}.
prf:q-resolvent-unique: Proof Proof of uniqueness of the q-resolvent. Standard: if R_1, R_2 are both two-sided inverses of s + \widehat{\Delta_q} in \mathrm{End}(\bigoplus V_j \otimes V_j^\vee), then R_1 = R_1 \circ (s + \widehat{\Delta_q}) \circ R_2 = R_2. Uniqueness holds isotypically (each summand has a unique scalar inverse (s + \lambda_j(q))^{-1}) and globally by direct sum.
rem:laplace-fourier-wick-rotation:
Remark Laplace and Fourier as Wick-rotated grouplike pairings. The categorical Laplace and categorical Fourier transforms are two real forms of a single complex spectral pairing against the q-exponential grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q):

  \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) \;=\; \mathcal{L}[f](i\xi).

This is the categorical Wick rotation. The q-heat equation \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u and the Schrödinger-type equation i\partial_t u = -\Delta_q u are sibling dynamics, evolving under \tau = t + i\varTheta. The Wick rotation acts only on the spectral parameter, securing base-ring independence where a primitive fourth root of unity exists.
prop:q-exp-entire:
Proposition The q-exponential is entire. Fix the aether regime q > 1 and write [n]_q = q^{n-1} + q^{n-3} + \cdots + q^{-(n-1)} for the balanced q-integer, with [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^{n} [k]_q. The q-exponential series

  \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!}

converges for every x \in \mathbb{C}; equivalently \exp_q is entire.

The proof is a ratio test. Dropping the positive tail of the balanced expansion gives [n+1]_q \ge q^{n}, so [n]_q! > 0 and the ratio of consecutive terms is \|x\| / [n+1]_q \le \|x\|\, q^{-n} \to 0; since q^n \to \infty the ratio is eventually below \tfrac12, so the series is summable.
prop:beta-eq-ln-q-dictionary:
Proposition The \beta = \ln q partition-function dictionary. Read the Frobenius/Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda} y_\lambda(q)\,\chi_\lambda as a statistical-mechanics partition function, with the Wedderburn blocks \lambda as microstates. At inverse temperature \beta = \ln q (positive for q > 1), each positive weight y_\lambda(q) is the Boltzmann weight of block \lambda, whose energy is

  E_\lambda = -\frac{\ln y_\lambda(q)}{\ln q}.

This energy is the unique solution of e^{-\beta E_\lambda} = y_\lambda, and it is order-reversing in the weight:

  E_{\lambda_1} \le E_{\lambda_2} \iff y_{\lambda_2} \le y_{\lambda_1},

so the dominant Wedderburn block — the one with the largest Frobenius weight — is the ground state. Summing the Boltzmann weights over the blocks with their degeneracies d_\lambda recovers the Frobenius weighted sum,

  \sum_{\lambda} d_\lambda\, e^{-\beta E_\lambda} = \sum_{\lambda} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda,

so the statistical-mechanics partition function written in energy variables and the Frobenius weighted sum are the same object in two bases.
prose:intro-q-special-functions: Three categorical special functions pair with the resolvent: the q-exponential \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q), its primitive inverse \log_q, and the level-2 iterated primitive \mathrm{Li}_2^q. Each is defined Hopf-algebraically, circumventing analytic representations.
def:q-exponential:
Definition q-Exponential (grouplike). A grouplike of the q-shuffle Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q is an element g \in \mathcal{H}_q satisfying \Delta_q(g) = g \otimes g and \epsilon(g) = 1. The q-exponential is the unique grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q) satisfying the categorical flow equation

  D_q  \exp_q  =  \exp_q, \qquad \exp_q(0) = 1.
rem:q-exponential-realisations:
Remark Realisations of \exp_q: universal property, base rings, the Habiro ring, and the Reeb flow. The q-exponential is the free grouplike on the primitive generator of the Reeb flow. Its Taylor coefficients lie in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}[\![x]\!]. Evaluation at any root of unity is the purely algebraic cyclotomic-projection \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q).

\exp_q operates as the categorical generator of the Reeb flow, dictating the q-deformed rotation \mathcal{L}_\xi Z = J\hbar_q Z on the aether coordinate Z.
prop:q-exponential-exists: Proposition Existence of the q-exponential grouplike. Let \mathcal{H}_q be the q-shuffle Hopf algebra over a base ring R in which the Jackson integers [n]_q are invertible. There exists a unique grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q) satisfying D_q \exp_q = \exp_q and \epsilon(\exp_q) = 1.
prf:q-exponential-exists:
Proof Proof of existence of the q-exponential grouplike. Over R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]\bigl[\tfrac{1}{[n]_q!} : n \ge 1\bigr] the element

  \exp_q \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!} \;\in\; \mathcal{H}_q

is grouplike (via the q-binomial identity \Delta_q(x^n) = \sum_{k} \binom{n}{k}_q x^k \otimes x^{n-k}) and flow-invariant (via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q x^{n-1}, which shifts the series by one index while preserving the sum). Over \mathbb{C}, the non-root-of-unity condition q \notin \mu_\infty (existence of aether parameter, Step 3) keeps each [n]_q! \ne 0, and the resulting series converges to the analytic q-exponential (the Taylor series of \exp_q, derived in the information-theory chapter). Over \mathbb{F}_p the hypothesis fails (the finite-field obstruction, remarked below); a truncated existence result holds modulo x^p = 0. Over \mathbb{Q}_p and \mathbb{C}_p existence follows from the Witt-vector lift (the p-adic \exp_q, remarked below).
prop:q-exponential-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the q-exponential grouplike (conditional). Conditional on flow rigidity. Let H be an additive abelian group whose counit \epsilon and q-Jackson derivative D_q are additive, and suppose the flow equation is rigid on H: an element fixed by D_q with vanishing counit is zero. Then any two grouplikes of \mathcal{H}_q sharing \epsilon and D_q coincide.

Both hypotheses are steps the accompanying proof already takes. Rigidity is its assertion that the flow equation on primitives has only the trivial solution; additivity is what lets it form the difference e_1 - e_2 and apply \epsilon and D_q to it. Given them, that difference is fixed by D_q and has counit 1 - 1 = 0, so it vanishes.

Discharging rigidity needs a graded q-shuffle Hopf algebra: the degree bound is what makes the coefficient-vanishing argument run.
prf:q-exponential-unique:
Proof Proof of uniqueness of the q-exponential grouplike. Assume the ambient counit and q-Jackson derivative are additive, and that the flow equation is rigid: an element fixed by D_q with vanishing counit is zero.

The difference e_1 - e_2 is fixed by D_q, since D_q is additive and each e_i satisfies D_q e_i = e_i; and its counit is \epsilon(e_1) - \epsilon(e_2) = 1 - 1 = 0. Rigidity gives e_1 - e_2 = 0.

Rigidity is where the content sits, and it is stated as a hypothesis rather than discharged. The expected argument is that iterating D_q on a primitive of bounded degree forces every coefficient but the leading one to vanish, and the counit condition kills the constant term — which needs a graded q-shuffle Hopf algebra, since the degree bound is what makes the iteration terminate.
rem:q-exp-finite-field-obstruction: Remark Finite-field obstruction for \exp_q. The archimedean Taylor series \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} x^n / [n]_q! fails over a field of characteristic p whenever the Jackson factorial [n]_q! vanishes modulo p. The grouplike \exp_q nonetheless exists as a symbol in the formal Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q \otimes \mathbb{F}_p. The truncated p-exponential \exp_q^{(p)}(x) = \sum_{n = 0}^{p - 1} x^n / [n]_q! becomes grouplike modulo x^p = 0.
